title: Kennedy’s Quiet Hunt for Autism Culprits Stalls as Trump Orders Baseless Changes to Childhood Shots
summary: The Trump administration is working to implement the president’s new order on childhood vaccines, which he publicly faulted for a rise in autism — even as health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s closed-door research has yet to produce evidence linking them.

title: Newsom Promotes Affordable Insulin, but California’s Generic Label Off to a Slow Start
summary: California is the first to launch state-branded insulin as Gov. Gavin Newsom tries to disrupt the pharmaceutical industry. But the new CalRx drug label has been slow to reach pharmacies and patients.

title: Gounder Brings Clarity to Egg Freezing, AI Virus Creation, and New Trump Vaccine Order
summary: KFF Health News editor-at-large for public health Céline Gounder made several TV appearances recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a roundup.

title: Trump Team’s Use of Arcane Budget Rule Threatens Medicaid Coverage
summary: Coverage for hundreds of thousands of Arkansas Medicaid enrollees next year is in question after the Trump administration refused to renew a key state waiver. The state might not be the last to have to adjust to an arcane rule change under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

title: My Husband Was Kicked Out of Hospice for Dying Too Slowly
summary: Some seriously ill patients improve on hospice. About 1 in 16 patients enrolled in hospice care lose eligibility as a result. Here’s how to get appropriate care after receiving a terminal diagnosis.

title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Readers Speak Out on Work Requirements, Federal Data Grab, Opioid Payback Cash
summary: KFF Health News gives readers a chance to comment on a recent batch of stories.

title: People With Disabilities Say Medicaid’s Limits on Income Stifle Career Advancement
summary: Special Medicaid programs in many states allow disabled people to work while receiving benefits, and most limit how much participants can earn and the assets they can hold. Some Iowans are pushing lawmakers to remove those limits, which they say can dampen their career prospects.

title: Years After He Quit Smoking, a Lung Cancer Scan Saved His Life
summary: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer deaths in the United States, and older adults are at higher risk. But only about a quarter of patients eligible for screening are up to date.

title: Hospitals Say They Found a Tool To Help Reduce Childbirth Risks: Wristbands
summary: North Carolina and other states have embraced “I Gave Birth” wristbands as a way to encourage women to seek help when they have postpartum complications. They’re gaining steam as the Trump administration’s cuts to Medicaid threaten postpartum care.
